findings.title: Missing content-security-policy header
findings.label: Script & content control (CSP)
findings.why: Controls what can load/run — the big one. Lock script-src to 'self'.
findings.plain: Your site doesn't tell browsers which scripts are allowed to run on it.
findings.impact: If an attacker ever sneaks code onto a page — through a comment box, an ad, or a compromised third-party script — nothing stops it from running. It could steal visitor data or deface the page, and visitors would have no way to tell.
findings.fixPlain: Add a Content-Security-Policy header that only allows scripts from your own domain.
findings.code: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'

findings.title: Missing strict-transport-security header
findings.label: Force-encrypt connections (HSTS)
findings.plain: Browsers aren't told to always use the encrypted (https://) version of your site.
findings.impact: A visitor's very first request — before HTTPS even kicks in, say on public wifi — could be quietly downgraded and read or tampered with by someone else on the network.
findings.fixPlain: Add a Strict-Transport-Security header so browsers go straight to HTTPS for your domain from then on.

findings.title: Missing x-content-type-options header
findings.label: File-type guessing lockdown
findings.plain: Browsers are left to guess what kind of file they're loading instead of trusting what you specify.
findings.impact: In older browsers, a malicious file disguised as an image could get executed as a script.

findings.title: Missing x-frame-options header
findings.label: Clickjacking protection
findings.plain: Nothing stops another website from loading your page inside an invisible frame.
findings.impact: This enables “clickjacking” — e.g. a fake “claim your prize” page could hide your real donate or login button underneath, so a visitor thinks they're clicking one thing and actually clicks another.
findings.fixPlain: Add an X-Frame-Options header (or a CSP frame-ancestors rule) so your pages can't be framed by other sites.

findings.title: Serve static assets with an efficient cache policy
findings.label: Serve static assets with an efficient cache policy
findings.fix: See the Lighthouse audit id for guidance.
findings.plain: Returning visitors re-download files that haven't changed.
findings.impact: Every repeat visit feels slower than it needs to, and costs you bandwidth.
findings.fixPlain: Tell the browser to cache images, CSS, and JS files for longer.
findings.tool: Set Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable on static assets. Netlify/Vercel: a _headers or vercel.json rule; Express: app.use(express.static(dir, { maxAge: '1y', immutable: true })).
findings.code:
# _headers file (Netlify / Cloudflare Pages):
/assets/*
  Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable

# Express:
app.use(express.static(dir, { maxAge: "1y", immutable: true }));

# Applies to, right now:
#   s.js

findings.title: Network dependency tree
findings.label: Network dependency tree
findings.why: Lighthouse flagged this as a performance opportunity.
findings.fix: See the Lighthouse audit id for guidance.
findings.plain: Loading one file forces the browser to wait, then request another, then another, in a chain.
findings.impact: Each link in that chain adds delay before the page is usable.
findings.fixPlain: Shorten the chain — preload key resources instead of letting the browser discover them late.
findings.tool: Chrome DevTools > Network tab, enable the waterfall view, to see the exact dependency chain.

findings.title: No structured data (JSON-LD) found
findings.label: Structured data
findings.why: No <script type="application/ld+json"> block was found on the page.
findings.fix: Add JSON-LD structured data for the page's type (Organization, LocalBusiness, Article, etc.).
findings.impact: No <script type="application/ld+json"> block was found on the page.
findings.fixPlain: Add JSON-LD structured data for the page's type (Organization, LocalBusiness, Article, etc.).

findings.title: Missing referrer-policy header
findings.label: Link-click privacy
findings.why: Limits what you leak in the Referer header.
findings.plain: When someone clicks a link off your site, their browser can leak the full page address they came from to whatever site they land on.
findings.impact: If any of your URLs ever contain something sensitive — a tracking token, a draft page name — that leaks to outside sites.
findings.fixPlain: Add a Referrer-Policy header (strict-origin-when-cross-origin is a safe default).

findings.title: Missing permissions-policy header
findings.label: Camera/mic/location lockdown
findings.plain: Browser features like camera, microphone, and location aren't explicitly turned off for your site.
findings.impact: A bug or a bad third-party script embedded on your page has access to more than it needs.
findings.fixPlain: Add a Permissions-Policy header that disables the features you don't use.

findings.title: server header reveals server details
findings.label: Server software disclosure
findings.why: If it names/versions the server, consider hiding it.
findings.fix: Remove or blank the `server` header (e.g. `app.disable('x-powered-by')` in Express).
findings.plain: Your server is naming or versioning itself in every response.
findings.impact: Same risk as above — it narrows down what an attacker needs to guess.
findings.fixPlain: Blank or shorten the Server header at your server or platform edge.
